name: Ivan Weber

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. Tell me what you do in a normal day.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and was made a junior manager of a six-person furniture-delivery complaints team last year. I worked on the shop floor for a long time before moving to the office, so I know when a wardrobe will not fit through a stairwell, but I am still learning staff budgets and the reporting system. I have a bachelor’s degree, not a management qualification. I like solving a customer’s problem, but my written reports take me longer than they take the experienced managers.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is life outside the office like now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner cleans offices on a changing roster, and our grown children live on their own. We rent a flat and have about three weeks of expenses saved. My pay is low for a manager, and there are not many similar jobs near us. I use the company’s AI drafting aid once in a while after someone else has tested it, then correct it against the delivery notes. Retirement is getting closer, but I have not checked what income we could actually live on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team AI Plateau might write a faster apology, but it will not carry a wardrobe up a narrow stair. The delivery note and the driver’s call must still decide what we offer a customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think the small software change will leave my new job mostly alone. I am less calm about the ordinary money: my partner’s cleaning shifts vary and we have less than a month saved. A lost week of their pay would put the rent in reach of the next cheque.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would keep my daily review of disputed delivery notes with the driver before I approve refunds. I would use the approved drafting aid only for straightforward letters and keep checking its dates against the log. If the mild change settles in next year, I would keep this routine and ask the payroll office for a clear record of my own retirement contributions, without assuming an amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about household cash even in this quiet version. The AI letter is not the thing that keeps me awake; a short cleaning roster is.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the driver tell you that the screen misses?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A delivery sheet said a wardrobe was refused, but the driver told me the upstairs landing was too narrow to turn it. The furniture customer had not simply changed their mind about the wardrobe; it could not turn on the upstairs landing. We sent a smaller model and paid for the return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you know about retirement income?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not enough. I know money is taken from my pay, but I have not checked the amount or the conditions. I will not tell my partner we can retire on a number I have never seen.

say: A **faster apology** cannot replace a driver’s account of a failed delivery.
I would use the **delivery note** to decide a fair remedy.
think: The **junior manager job** looks mostly stable in a mild scenario.
My partner’s **variable cleaning shifts** and three-week reserve put rent at risk.
do: **Use** the approved drafting aid only on routine letters, checking dates.
**Request** an actual record of retirement contributions from payroll.
feel: I feel **anxious** about rent when cleaning shifts are short.
S0.quote: The furniture customer had not simply changed their mind about the wardrobe; it could not turn on the upstairs landing.
fieldNote: His **baseline money worry** comes from variable partner hours and less than one month saved.
He makes no **retirement entitlement** claim before checking the payroll record.

steps.text: Keep checking disputed delivery notes with driver before refunds
Use approved drafting aid only for checked routine letters

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say Steady Disruption can take routine complaint letters and refund checks, and the company should bargain over the time it saves. I would take real errors to our union branch, not ask drivers to absorb them for free.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Between us, our office may need fewer people, and I am the least experienced manager there. My delivery knowledge might help, but it does not make my low-paid post safe. Three weeks saved will not carry the rent through a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask the union representative to put a paid complaints-checking role and notice terms on the next meeting agenda. I would check one week of AI-drafted refunds against driver notes on paid time if my manager approves that time. If a local returns-clerk vacancy is posted, I would apply only after seeing that its take-home pay and travel cost cover the rent; I would accept only an actual offer with workable shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about being the easiest manager to cut. I would rather show the branch a wrong refund than make a speech about machines.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a wrong refund?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A system might refund a delivery fee when the actual damage was to a table leg. The customer still needs a repair or replacement. I would put the photograph and the driver note beside the automated decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a clerk wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the money left after travel pays our rent and basics. My partner’s cleaning weeks are not steady enough to fill a gap. A job advert is a place to ask, not a cheque.

say: **Routine complaints** may be automated, and staff should bargain over saved time.
I would bring **refund errors** to the union branch.
think: My **junior post** may be easier to cut than experienced managers’ posts.
A **three-week reserve** cannot fund a long search.
do: **Ask** union representative for paid checking work and notice terms next month.
**Check** one week of AI refunds against driver notes only with manager-approved paid time.
**Apply** to posted local returns work only if net pay after travel covers rent and basics.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible cut and want evidence for bargaining.
S1.quote: A job advert is a place to ask, not a cheque.
fieldNote: His **delivery experience** helps identify errors but does not erase his junior standing.
The **returns application** has a rent-and-travel gate; no post or wage is guaranteed.

steps.text: Ask union representative for paid complaint-checking work and notice terms
Check AI refunds against driver notes only on approved paid time
Apply for posted returns job only if net pay after travel covers rent
Accept only actual offer with rent-covering pay and workable shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union AGI by 2028 could settle complaints and write our reports before the company has a fair plan for us. We need written notice, severance figures and a real way for a driver or customer to challenge a wrong result.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect this small complaints office to lose posts quickly, and my own junior job may go. A returns-clerk desk is thinking work too and faces 2028 AGI. Carrying furniture is physical until capable robots around 2031, but I cannot assume a warehouse vacancy or a wage that meets our rent. We have only three weeks saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would bring the union branch a list of unresolved damage claims and ask it to seek written notice and appeal rules. I would check our rent and food dates with my partner before any final pay cheque arrives. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would apply for advertised local delivery-support work only with net pay and travel costs that meet rent and basics; I would take only a confirmed offer and real shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about how little time our savings would buy if my wage stopped. I am not giving up, but we cannot finance a long experiment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could the grown children cover a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own homes and bills. I would tell them what happened, but I would not write their wages into our rent plan. Our first call would be to the union about what the company actually owes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a driver challenge look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The driver should be able to show a photograph of the damaged leg and have a person reopen the refund. A computer closing the complaint does not mend the customer’s table. Someone needs the authority to change the answer.

say: **2028 AGI** could close complaints before staff have fair notice.
I would demand **appeal rules** for drivers and customers.
think: My **junior post** may go as the complaints office shrinks.
Returns desks face **2028 AGI**; physical furniture handling meets robots around 2031.
do: **Bring** unresolved damage claims to the union this week for notice and appeal demands.
**Check** rent and food due dates with my partner before any final pay.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only to advertised work with rent-covering net pay after travel and real shifts.
feel: I feel **alarmed** because three weeks saved cannot cover a long wage gap.
S2.quote: A computer closing the complaint does not mend the customer’s table.
fieldNote: His **three-week reserve** and expected office cuts explain alarm without assuming grown children subsidise him.
He knows **returns desks** are also exposed to 2028 AGI, while robots follow around 2031.

steps.text: Give union unresolved damage claims and seek written notice and appeal rules
Apply after cut to advertised delivery-support roles only with rent-covering net pay after travel
Take only confirmed offer with verified shifts and basic bills covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to demand paid learning on real damage claims, not a brochure about being flexible. I would ask the company and union to set a named appeal worker who can reopen a case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I might be able to learn furniture damage inspection before 2031, but it needs supervised practice because I do not yet judge repairs well. Complaint reports and inspection paperwork face 2031 AGI; physical handling robots follow around 2034. At 63 I cannot rely on a retirement cheque until I have checked its actual rules, and our reserve remains thin.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I would request two paid inspection mornings a month with the repair supervisor, but I would go only if my complaints manager covers the queue and the supervisor agrees to mark my work. I would enrol in a repair-assessment course only if an actual place, funded fee and paid working hours are approved. After 2031 I would apply only to a posted inspection role with verified net rent pay and hours I can manage; a course would not itself be a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because five years could let me learn, but our rent cannot wait for unpaid training. I am not sure how much physical lifting I would manage at 63.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the repair supervisor mark?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether the table leg can be repaired, what a replacement costs and which photograph proves the damage happened during delivery. I have seen many furniture claims but have never signed a damage inspection. A supervisor would need to tell me when I got the cause wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you borrow for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We have less than a month saved, and a loan would make the rent more fragile. I would accept funded learning with paid hours, not a debt for a job that may never be posted.

say: A **five-year runway** should fund supervised damage-inspection learning.
I would seek a named **appeal worker** with reopening authority.
think: Inspection reports face **2031 AGI**, and handling robots follow around 2034.
At **63**, my retirement income remains unverified and savings remain thin.
do: **Request** two paid monthly inspection mornings in 2027; attend only with complaints-queue cover and supervisor agreement to mark work.
**Enrol** in repair assessment only with an actual place, funded fee and paid working hours.
**Apply** after 2031 only for posted inspection work with verified rent-covering net pay and manageable hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about unpaid training and uncertain physical capacity at 63.
S3.quote: I have seen many furniture claims but have never signed a damage inspection.
fieldNote: His **inspection plan** is conditional on paid supervised practice, not claimed expertise.
A **course place** needs fee and wage cover; any later job also needs a real vacancy and rent pay.

steps.text: Request two paid monthly inspections; attend only with queue cover and supervisor marking work
Enrol in offered repair course only with funded fee and paid working hours
Apply after 2031 only to posted inspection role with rent-covering net pay and manageable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company a decade is time to agree on notice, appeal rights and paid apprenticeships, especially for older staff who cannot start over for free. I would ask the union to see the real cost before anyone promises a transition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I would be 68 by 2036. Perhaps I could retire, but I have not checked our pension or any other entitlement and cannot assume it will pay the rent. Complaint and inspection paperwork face 2036 AGI; physical delivery and repairs meet robots around 2039. Our three-week reserve is a problem even with ten years to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the delivery-note checks now and request an exact retirement-income statement this winter, then compare it with our rent and food costs with my partner. I would put twenty extra into savings only in months when both wages arrive and rent and utilities are paid. After 2036 I would stay employed if the work and pay remain real; I would stop only if verified retirement income plus savings can cover our bills, and otherwise apply for an advertised job with manageable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious despite the longer runway because ten years does not fill an empty savings account by itself. I would like to retire someday, but I cannot call it a plan without numbers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens if the statement is too small?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep working while I could and ask the union what notice and training the company must actually provide. Our grown children have their own costs. I do not want to tell my grown children they owe us a retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why only twenty saved?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On my wage and my partner’s uneven cleaning roster, twenty is sometimes what is left after rent. I would transfer it from a full-pay month, not pretend we can save it when a shift is cancelled. We would revisit the amount if wages change.

say: A **decade** should bring notice, appeals and paid learning for older staff.
I would ask the **union** to price any promised transition.
think: At **68**, retirement income is unknown and cannot be counted on for rent.
Desk reports face **2036 AGI**, with physical delivery robots around 2039.
do: **Request** an actual retirement-income statement and compare it with rent and food.
**Save** twenty extra only after both wages arrive and rent and utilities clear.
**Stay** employed if work and pay remain; stop after 2036 only if verified income plus savings cover bills, otherwise apply.
feel: I feel **anxious** because ten years alone does not build a cash reserve.
S4.quote: I do not want to tell my grown children they owe us a retirement.
fieldNote: He treats **retirement income** as unknown until a real statement and eligibility terms are checked.
His **twenty transfer** adds new earnings only after full wages and essential bills.

steps.text: Save twenty only after both wages and paid rent and utilities
Stay employed after 2036 unless verified retirement income plus savings cover bills
Apply for advertised manageable work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Three weeks of savings cannot carry our rent if the complaints office closes quickly. Written notice, a real appeal job and paid supervised learning would help, but I would need to see a vacancy and the wage before counting it.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what an older worker is actually entitled to before telling us to retire. I have not checked my own figures yet. My grown children are not a line in our rent budget.

headlineQuote: My grown children are not a line in our rent budget.
portrait: **Ivan, 58**, is a junior complaints manager for a large furniture company, still learning budgets after shop-floor work.
His **lower wage**, cleaning-partner shifts, three-week reserve and few local posts leave rent exposed.
He uses **AI occasionally** for checked routine letters and asks the union for real appeal rights.
He is **anxious** even under mild change, alarmed by fast cuts and unwilling to assume retirement income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close his junior complaints post with only three weeks saved to cover rent and food.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, actual appeal authority and funded supervised learning with paid hours would help.
